messages.content: Quick Minneapolis update: the client just moved Thursday's wrap-up from noon to 2:00 p.m. Can you check whether my current flight home still works, and what it would cost to change it if not?

If the meeting really runs until 2:00 in Eden Prairie, the current 2:20 p.m. MSP-ATL return is not workable; it would require leaving before the wrap-up. The clean replacement I see is a Delta nonstop around 5:55 p.m., arriving ATL about 9:25 p.m. No change fee is showing, but the fare difference is about +$88. A cheaper one-stop saves roughly $45 compared with that, but gets in after 11 and adds connection risk.
That's pretty clear. Can you also keep an eye on not accidentally changing the hotel? I still need the Home2 reservation.

Yes. This would be a flight-only change; Home2 Suites Feb 10-13 stays as is. I would label the reason as client agenda shift and attach the fare difference, so approval knows the hotel nights are unchanged.
Is there any realistic way to keep the 2:20 if I do not check a bag?

I would not recommend it. Eden Prairie to MSP is usually 25-35 minutes without a bad traffic pocket, so even leaving at 2:00 puts you at the airport after the flight has closed. No checked bag does not fix the timing.
Okay, move the recommendation to the evening nonstop. Before I send it, can we verify late-arrival handling at the hotel in case Monday travel gets delayed?

For Home2, the front desk is listed as 24 hours and the reservation is guaranteed by card, so they should hold the room. Add a late-arrival note for any arrival after 10 p.m.; also use mobile check-in if the Hilton app offers it. I would still confirm the cancellation deadline in the booking tool.
Can you give me the final text for the change request?

Change request note: Client moved Thursday wrap-up to 2:00 p.m., making the current 2:20 p.m. MSP-ATL return unworkable. Please change only the return flight to the Delta nonstop around 5:55 p.m. MSP-ATL, arriving about 9:25 p.m. Current display shows no change fee and about an $88 fare difference. Hotel remains Home2 Suites Minneapolis-Eden Prairie, Feb 10-13. Add late-arrival note to the hotel reservation in case Monday travel is delayed; front desk appears to be 24 hours.

messages.content: Minneapolis is finally not occupying my brain. Can we start sketching DC for spring break? It would be me, my spouse, and our kid, mostly museums, five days or so from Atlanta.

Sure. To map it cleanly, I need the school break window, whether you want to consider all three DC-area airports or only the most convenient one, and a rough hotel comfort target. I can start by comparing flight timing against museum-friendly neighborhoods near Metro.

Break is April 7-11. We could leave Friday April 4 after school or Saturday morning, and come back Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday. Nonstop if fares are reasonable, and I do not want a first night that starts with landing at 11 p.m.

For a museum-heavy trip, Reagan National is the practical airport if the price is close: short Metro or rideshare into the core. Dulles and BWI can work, but the transfer eats into a short trip. Date-wise, Friday evening to Tuesday gives you four nights and three full-ish days; Saturday to Wednesday is calmer but shifts the first museum day later.
Can you compare Friday evening versus Saturday morning flights, assuming we aim for Reagan first?

A first pass: Friday ATL-DCA nonstops after school tend to be around 6:00-7:30 p.m., landing roughly 8:00-9:15, often the priciest bucket. Saturday morning nonstops usually run a little cheaper and land before lunch, but you lose the easy Friday settle-in. If DCA is more than about $100 per person higher than IAD or BWI, I would at least look at the other airport; below that, DCA's convenience likely wins.
Connections are probably not worth it unless the savings are huge. What hotel areas should I compare?

I would compare four zones: Penn Quarter/Convention Center for easy Metro and walkable dinners; National Mall/L'Enfant or the Wharf for closest museum access but sometimes higher rates; Dupont/Farragut for a calmer evening neighborhood with Metro; and Arlington spots like Crystal City or Rosslyn for lower rates with a Metro ride in.
Room needs to fit three comfortably. Breakfast helps if it is included, and I want solid reviews, say 4-ish or better. Not luxury, just not a tired property.

Good targets. In the core, look at Embassy Suites Convention Center for more room and breakfast, Residence Inn Downtown/Convention Center for breakfast and apartment-style layouts, and Hampton Inn Convention Center if the rate is better. For a value option, Residence Inn or Hampton in Crystal City can be much cheaper and still Metro-accessible, but morning rides to the Mall take longer.
Would staying near the Mall save us enough time to justify the higher price?

Sometimes, but not always. With a child, being near a Metro station matters more than being able to walk to every museum. A Convention Center or Penn Quarter hotel can get you to the Mall quickly and gives easier dinner options at night. I would pay a moderate premium for that, but not $150 more per night over a solid Arlington option.
What about the Wharf? It looks fun.

The Wharf is good for evenings and waterfront restaurants, and L'Enfant Plaza access is useful. The tradeoff is that some hotels are a longer walk to the Metro and rates can jump. It works well if you find a breakfast-included room at a reasonable rate; otherwise Convention Center is usually simpler for museum mornings.
If we fly into DCA, how bad is it to get to those areas with luggage?

DCA is very manageable. Rideshare to Penn Quarter or the Convention Center is often 15-25 minutes depending on traffic. Metro is also workable, though with a child and bags I would use rideshare on arrival and Metro for the rest of the trip.
Could we fly into DCA and return from IAD or BWI if that saves money?

Yes, but I would only split airports for a meaningful savings. Returning from IAD or BWI adds more transfer planning, and on a short family trip that can erase some fare savings. If the difference is under roughly $250-$300 total for the three of you, I would keep DCA both ways.
Can you ballpark total cost so I can decide if we are doing core or Arlington?

Roughly: three nonstop DCA tickets might land around $900-$1,150 total depending on dates. Four core hotel nights could be about $1,200-$1,600 with taxes; Arlington might be $800-$1,100. So the all-in difference before food and activities may be $300-$600, mostly hotel-driven.
Okay. Spouse has to confirm which days he can take off. Give me a short version I can send him, with what is still unknown.

Send this: DC spring break plan is best framed around ATL-DCA nonstops if fares stay reasonably close to IAD/BWI, because Reagan keeps arrival and museum logistics simpler. Most likely date patterns are Friday evening to Tuesday for four nights, or Saturday morning to Wednesday for a calmer but slightly later start. Hotel areas to compare are Convention Center/Penn Quarter for the best balance, Wharf/L'Enfant if rates are competitive, and Crystal City/Rosslyn if saving several hundred dollars matters more. Still unknown: exact travel dates, flight fare gap by airport, hotel nightly budget, room type for three, breakfast inclusion, cancellation terms, and whether museum-area convenience beats a cheaper Metro ride from Arlington.

messages.content: Spouse confirmed: we can leave after school Friday April 4 and come back Tuesday April 8 after lunch. Prices look higher than when we first talked. Can you recompare flights and the two hotel finalists?

Here is the narrowed view. Option A is ATL-DCA nonstop Friday about 6:15 p.m. to 7:58 p.m., returning Tuesday about 1:45 p.m. to 3:39 p.m., around $371 per person; best schedule. Option B is Saturday morning to Tuesday, around $309 per person; it saves airfare and one hotel night but shortens the trip. Option C is Friday into IAD, around $326 per person; cheaper, but the arrival transfer is longer. Option D is a one-stop around $268 per person; meaningful savings, but it turns the after-school travel day into a connection.
Which airline is option A? If Delta is close I lean that way, but schedule matters more for this one.

Two close DCA nonstops are available. American is around 6:15 p.m.-7:58 p.m. outbound and 1:45 p.m.-3:39 p.m. return, about $371 per person. Delta is around 6:40 p.m.-8:29 p.m. outbound and 2:05 p.m.-3:58 p.m. return, about $382 per person. American lands earlier and is a little cheaper; Delta is still reasonable if the seat map or loyalty value matters.
Let's not land later just for the carrier. American sounds fine unless there is some catch.
No obvious catch from the comparison: both are nonstop, return after lunch, and neither runs into late evening. I would choose American here because the earlier arrival helps the first night.
For hotels, we were looking at Residence Inn Convention Center and Embassy Suites Convention Center, right?

Yes. Residence Inn Downtown/Convention Center is showing about $269 per night refundable before taxes, strong guest reviews, breakfast listed, and studio layouts with sofa bed. Embassy Suites Convention Center is about $296 per night, breakfast listed, more separation in the room, and a family-friendly setup. Embassy costs about $120-$140 more over the stay after taxes.
Does Residence Inn's breakfast look definite? That would make mornings easier.

The refundable rate page lists complimentary breakfast, but I would still verify it on the final checkout screen because some third-party displays are sloppy. Also confirm the room occupancy shows three guests and not just two adults.
What if we shift to Saturday morning? The airfare is lower and we'd drop a hotel night.

Saturday-Tuesday would probably save about $500 total: roughly $180-$220 on airfare plus one hotel night with tax. The tradeoff is losing the relaxed Friday arrival and most of Saturday as a museum day. If budget pressure is the main issue, Saturday is the cleanest savings lever; if the trip should feel less squeezed, Friday is better.
Keep Friday. I would rather not squeeze it too much.

Then the booking path I recommend is: book the Friday ATL-DCA nonstop and Tuesday early-afternoon DCA-ATL return now, using the American itinerary unless its seat map is poor. Hold the Residence Inn refundable rate, and switch to Embassy Suites only if the suite space is worth the extra amount when you see the final tax total.
Please write the booking note and list what I need to verify before I click purchase.

Booking note: Family DC spring-break trip for three, April 4-8. Book ATL-DCA nonstop Friday evening after school and DCA-ATL Tuesday early afternoon. Current lead is American at about $371 per person because it lands earlier than the comparable Delta option and keeps the return after lunch. Avoid IAD/BWI or a one-stop unless the final savings become much larger. Hotel lead is Residence Inn Washington, DC Downtown/Convention Center, refundable rate around $269 per night before taxes, room for three, breakfast listed, near Metro. Verify before purchase: traveler names and birthdates, seat availability together, baggage rules, flight change/cancellation terms, final fare total, hotel breakfast on the checkout page, cancellation deadline, room type with sofa bed or two beds, occupancy for three, and total taxes or destination fees.
